page: Amazon Web Services c7g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the custom 64-core AWS Graviton3 processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture. Operating at 2.6 GHz, the instance features 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating simultaneous multithreading overhead. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The underlying virtualization is managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. There is no local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration bundled with this instance type, and network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieved a strong multi-core stress-ng CPU score of 97,859.32 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,590.0, while single-core metrics for both suites remain in the average tier. Memory performance is notable, with Passmark memory scores and cached read bandwidth of 6,198.84 GB/sec placing in the top tier. Software compilation with Clang also registered a top-tier Geekbench score of 58,963.0. For database and key-value workloads, the server processed 100.88 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved a strong Passmark database score.

Tradeoffs are present in cryptographic and vector processing capabilities, as the Neoverse-V1 architecture lacks AVX, AVX-512, and AMX instruction sets, though it supports AES cryptography. LLM inference benchmarks show mixed results: while text generation for medium (7B) models is strong at 31.32 tokens/sec, text generation for small (135M) models is weak at 64.46 tokens/sec. Given the 1:2 resource density and strong multi-threaded performance, this server is suited for CPU-bound workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, multi-threaded data processing, and Redis-based caching layers.
